battle.name: 第二次巴爾干戰爭
battle.brief: 第二次巴爾干戰爭於1913年6月爆發，保加利亞與塞爾維亞、希臘、門塔內哥及羅馬尼亞聯軍交戰，戰線集中於馬其頓與色雷斯；保加利亞軍曾使用別丹步槍（Berdan rifle），此型步槍於1866年即已列裝。

kit.name: 別丹步槍
kit.history: 別丹步槍是俄羅斯帝國陸軍的制式步槍，配發於步兵與後備部隊，後來仍見於蘇聯軍方的舊式裝備體系。

countries: 1913年的第二次巴爾干戰爭中，保加利亞是主要進攻方；另一方起初是塞爾維亞與希臘，黑山於7月2日宣戰加入，羅馬尼亞則在8月10日參戰。戰場沿三條彼此銜接而指揮獨立的戰線展開：塞保線由尼什經皮羅特、弗拉涅與庫什泰利向瓦爾達爾河上游延伸；希保線由薩洛尼卡東南經基爾基斯、拉哈納斯、德米爾希薩爾通往塞雷斯；黑山軍則由桑扎克向塞爾維亞邊境施壓。羅馬尼亞最後由北多布魯加南進，使保加利亞同時承受西、南、北三面壓力。鄂圖曼帝國仍控制君士坦丁堡與西色雷，沒有加入交戰方。
countriesEn: In the Second Balkan War of 1913, Bulgaria was the principal attacker; its opponents were initially Serbia and Greece, Montenegro declared war and entered on 2 July, and Romania entered on 10 August. The battlefield developed along three connected but independently commanded fronts: the Serbian-Bulgarian line ran from Niš through Pirot, Vranje and Kustendil toward the upper Vardar; the Greek-Bulgarian line ran southeast from Salonika through Kilkis, Lachanas and Demir Hisar toward Serres; and the Montenegrin army pressed from Sandžak toward the Serbian frontier. Romania finally advanced from northern Dobruja, placing Bulgaria under pressure from the west, south and north at once. The Ottoman Empire still controlled Constantinople and eastern Thrace and did not join the belligerents.
people: 最高決策與前線指揮分屬不同層級。保加利亞國王費迪南德一世拒絕接受倫敦會議對馬其頓的安排，首相迪米塔爾·通切夫主持最後談判，至7月2日改由萊科·達斯凱洛夫組閣；格奧爾基·瓦西列夫、弗拉基米爾·瓦佐夫等將領分率前線集團軍。塞爾維亞國王彼得一世和首相尼古拉·帕希奇決定堅守新得的馬其頓，總參謀長約萬·米什科維奇負責整體軍務，沃伊斯拉夫·普特尼克指揮主要野戰方向。希臘的埃萊夫塞里奧斯·韋尼澤洛斯主張以薩洛尼卡為基地，國王康斯坦丁一世掌最高軍事權，王儲康斯坦丁統率泰薩利方面，潘約季奧蒂斯·孔多焦爾吉斯負責馬其頓戰區。黑山由尼古拉一世與首相揚科·武科蒂奇主持；羅馬尼亞則由卡羅爾一世、首相蒂圖·馬約雷斯庫及多布魯加戰區指揮官伊昂·德拉加利納決定介入時機。俄國外相謝爾蓋·薩宗諾夫則以勸止戰事擴大、促成停火為主要外交目標。
peopleEn: Strategic decisions and front command operated at different levels. Tsar Ferdinand I of Bulgaria rejected the London settlement on Macedonia; Prime Minister Dimitar Tonchev conducted the final negotiations and was replaced on 2 July by Rayko Daskalov, while generals such as Georgi Vasilev and Vladimir Vazov commanded field formations. King Peter I of Serbia and Prime Minister Nikola Pašić resolved to retain the newly acquired Macedonian territory; Chief of the General Staff Jovan Mišković directed overall military planning, and Voislav Putnik commanded the principal operational directions. In Greece, Eleftherios Venizelos made Salonika the base of operations; King Constantine I held supreme military authority, Crown Prince Constantine commanded in Thessaly, and Panagiotis Kontogiorgis handled the Macedonian theatre. King Nicholas I and Prime Minister Janko Vukotić led Montenegro’s war effort, while King Carol I, Prime Minister Titu Maiorescu and Dobruja commander Ion Dragalina determined when Romania would intervene. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Sazonov chiefly sought to prevent wider escalation and obtain an armistice.
kits: 各軍裝備並非完全同型，以下只列1913年以前已正式列裝、且在1913年確有使用的代表型號。保加利亞步兵以7.92×57毫米曼利歇M1895步槍為主，採五發固定彈匣；塞爾維亞步兵主要使用7×39毫米R佩伊瑟M1907步槍，設十發彈匣；希臘軍大量配發曼利歇M1895；羅馬尼亞使用6.5×54毫米R斯特朗伯格M1901步槍，並保留曼利歇M1888/90；黑山軍常見馬丁尼－亨利M1871步槍。炮兵方面，保加利亞有75毫米施耐德－克雷梭M1906與120毫米施耐德M1906野戰炮，塞爾維亞有75毫米施耐德－克雷梭M1907及120毫米施耐德M1906，希臘有75毫米施耐德－克雷梭M1906和克魯普M1904，羅馬尼亞有75毫米克魯普M1904與施耐德－克雷梭M1907。各國75毫米炮配同口徑炮彈、隨屬炮車及馬匹挽具，機槍以Maxim M1904及其後續M1910為代表。步槍彈藥按7.92、7毫米及6.5毫米口徑分裝，炮兵彈藥由軍械隊以彈藥車送至炮位；野戰縱隊仍須依賴道路、畜力車與鐵路轉運。
kitsEn: The armies were not uniformly equipped, so the following are representative models formally adopted before 1913 and demonstrably in service during that year. Bulgarian infantry relied chiefly on the 7.92×57 mm Mannlicher M1895 rifle with a five-round fixed magazine; Serbian infantry primarily used the 7×39 mm R Peiser M1907 rifle with a ten-round magazine; Greek forces also received large quantities of Mannlicher M1895 rifles; Romania used the 6.5×54 mm R Ștrandberg M1901 and retained Mannlicher M1888/90 rifles; the Montenegrin army commonly used Martini-Henry M1871 rifles. Bulgarian artillery included the 75 mm Schneider-Creusot M1906 and 120 mm Schneider M1906 field guns; Serbia fielded the 75 mm Schneider-Creusot M1907 and 120 mm Schneider M1906; Greece used the 75 mm Schneider-Creusot M1906 and Krupp M1904; and Romania employed the 75 mm Krupp M1904 and Schneider-Creusot M1907. Each 75 mm gun had matching ammunition, a limber and horse-drawn transport; Maxim M1904 and the later M1910 were representative machine guns. Rifle ammunition was separated by the 7.92, 7 mm and 6.5 mm calibres, while artillery ammunition reached gun positions in ammunition wagons. Field columns still depended on roads, animal-drawn carts and railways for supply.
tactics: 六月二十日前後，希臘軍在保加利亞守軍撤出後進入薩洛尼卡，沒有為奪城發生重大交鋒，隨即以該港和相連道路作為後勤中心。6月29日，保加利亞同時在多個方向出擊：一路越過塞保邊界向斯科普里與庫什泰利壓進，一路在皮羅特、弗拉涅一帶攻擊，另一路由基爾基斯、德米爾希薩爾向馬其頓內地展開。塞軍利用道路、隘口與既設陣地遲滯正面攻勢，再以新集結的步兵和75毫米炮在斯科普里、克雷什納山口及布雷加爾尼察河一帶實施反擊；七月上旬塞軍奪回斯科普里，至七月下旬控制瓦爾達爾河中游和什蒂普。希臘軍則由薩洛尼卡向基爾基斯、拉哈納斯平行推進，以炮兵壓制道路、步兵占領高地，再由縱隊切斷保軍退路；基爾基斯－拉哈納斯戰鬥後，比托拉方向的保軍也被逐退。希軍七月下旬占領卡瓦拉與德米爾希薩爾一帶，八月初進抵塞雷斯，曾準備向阿德里安堡方向推進，但未奪取該城。各次交戰仍出現胸牆、機槍封鎖與短距離反擊，但勝負往往取決於鐵路、橋梁、城鎮與補給線能否控制。8月10日，羅馬尼亞自北多布魯加越過多瑙河攻入保境，迫使保軍把原本分散的預備隊再往北調動；同日簽訂條約後，各軍依指定路線撤出戰區。
tacticsEn: Around 20 June, after the Bulgarian garrison had withdrawn, Greek troops entered Salonika without a major struggle for the city and immediately established the port and its connecting roads as a supply centre. On 29 June Bulgaria attacked in several directions: one force crossed the Serbian frontier toward Skopje and Kustendil, another struck around Pirot and Vranje, and another expanded from Kilkis and Demir Hisar into the Macedonian interior. The Serbian army delayed frontal attacks by using roads, defiles and prepared positions, then counterattacked with newly concentrated infantry and 75 mm guns around Skopje, the Kresna Gorge and the Bregalnica River. Serbian troops retook Skopje in early July and by late July controlled the middle Vardar and Štip. The Greek army advanced in parallel from Salonika toward Kilkis and Lachanas, used artillery to dominate the roads, occupied heights with infantry and sent columns to cut Bulgarian retreat routes. After the fighting at Kilkis and Lachanas, the Bulgarian troops in the Bitola direction were also driven back. Greek forces took Kavala and the Demir Hisar area in late July, reached Serres in early August and prepared to advance toward Adrianople, but never captured that city. Breastworks, machine-gun positions and short counterattacks still appeared in individual engagements, yet outcomes frequently turned on control of railways, bridges, towns and supply routes. On 10 August Romania crossed the Danube from northern Dobruja into Bulgaria, forcing the Bulgarians to shift already dispersed reserves northward. After the treaty was signed that day, the armies withdrew along the prescribed routes.
data: 主要交戰自6月29日延至8月10日，羅馬尼亞戰線的作戰及各方撤軍則延至8月下旬。5月30日《倫敦條約》劃定第一次巴爾干戰爭後的邊界；6月19日保加利亞向塞爾維亞與希臘提出最後通牒；6月20日前後希臘軍進入薩洛尼卡；6月29日保軍發動全面攻擊；7月2日黑山宣戰。斯科普里戰鬥延續至7月6日，最後由塞軍收復該城。7月3日至10日是克雷什納山口戰鬥，塞軍取得勝利；7月4日至18日基爾基斯－拉哈納斯戰鬥由希軍取勝；7月8日至21日布雷加爾尼察戰鬥同樣以塞軍控制瓦爾達爾河中游告終；7月10日至18日比托拉戰鬥則由希軍占領比托拉。7月19日保加利亞提出停火要求，8月10日羅馬尼亞參戰並在布加勒斯特簽約，8月18日羅軍占領圖爾圖卡亞。常見的開戰兵力概略估計為保加利亞約三十萬、塞爾維亞約二十五萬、希臘約十三萬，黑山為數萬；羅馬尼亞在北方戰區實際投入約十六萬至二十餘萬，不同來源對動員人數與前線人數的算法不同。這些只是概括值而非單一名冊；各國對死傷、被俘、失聯及疾病的統計口徑不一，故不列未經一致核實的精確傷亡總數。海上沒有爆發決定性的主力艦隊交戰，希臘海軍維持薩洛尼卡航線，保加利亞黑海分隊則未能改變馬其頓岸段的陸戰局勢。
dataEn: The main hostilities lasted from 29 June to 10 August, while fighting on the Romanian front and the withdrawal of the armies continued into late August. The London Treaty fixed the post-First Balkan War frontier on 30 May; Bulgaria delivered its final ultimatum to Serbia and Greece on 19 June; Greek troops entered Salonika around 20 June; and Bulgaria launched its general offensive on 29 June. Montenegro declared war on 2 July. The fighting for Skopje continued until 6 July, when Serbian forces recovered the city. The Serbian victory at the Kresna Gorge ran from 3 to 10 July, the Greek victory at Kilkis-Lachanas from 4 to 18 July, and the Serbian victory in the Bregalnica fighting from 8 to 21 July gave Serbia control of the middle Vardar. The Greek victory at Bitola lasted from 10 to 18 July. Bulgaria requested an armistice on 19 July; Romania entered the war and signed at Bucharest on 10 August; and Romanian troops occupied Turtucaia on 18 August. Common estimates place the opening forces at roughly 300,000 for Bulgaria, 250,000 for Serbia and 130,000 for Greece, with Montenegro numbering several tens of thousands. Between about 160,000 and more than 200,000 Romanian troops were committed in the northern theatre, depending on whether total mobilization or front-line strength is counted. These are approximations rather than a single verified roll. National records used different definitions for casualties, prisoners, missing personnel and illness, so no precise combined casualty total is given here. No decisive engagement between the principal fleets occurred at sea; the Greek navy maintained the sea route to Salonika, while the Bulgarian Black Sea detachment could not alter the land campaign along the Macedonian coast.
cause: 直接原因是保加利亞不接受《倫敦條約》所確定的馬其頓安排，並企圖在希臘完全鞏固薩洛尼卡、塞爾維亞把新得地區納入軍用交通之前先行改變現狀。條約使保加利亞取得皮林馬其頓與阿德里安堡，卻把北馬其頓交給塞爾維亞、南馬其頓交給希臘，保加利亞既未取得通往愛琴海的完整出口，也未能打通從本土到亞得里亞海沿岸的鐵路走廊。6月19日，保加利亞向塞爾維亞提出歸還大部分北馬其頓的要求，向希臘提出放棄薩洛尼卡與南馬其頓、並放棄進一步索取阿德里安堡的要求。這些要求直接碰到塞、希兩國在第一次巴爾干戰爭中最核心的收穫，因此遭到拒絕。塞爾維亞還須防止保軍沿瓦爾達爾河切斷斯科普里與塞爾維亞本土的聯繫；希臘則要確保薩洛尼卡、卡瓦拉及通往南部馬其頓的交通；黑山希望重新取得桑扎克與梅托希亞。羅馬尼亞另有對奧匈帝國南特蘭西瓦尼亞的既有領土要求，戰局一旦失控，它便取得以多瑙加為界向保加利亞施壓的機會。德國與奧匈帝國在外交上支持保加利亞，俄國則擔心戰火擴及君士坦丁堡而著重勸止；鄂圖曼帝國在歐洲的削弱，也使保住阿德里安堡與阻止希臘向東推進成為各方軍事安排中的重要因素。
causeEn: The immediate cause was Bulgaria’s refusal to accept the Macedonian settlement established by the London Treaty and its attempt to change the situation before Greece fully consolidated Salonika and Serbia incorporated its new territories into the military transport system. The treaty gave Bulgaria Pirin Macedonia and Adrianople, but assigned northern Macedonia to Serbia and southern Macedonia to Greece; Bulgaria therefore received neither an unimpeded outlet to the Aegean nor a continuous railway corridor from its interior to the Adriatic coast. On 19 June Bulgaria demanded that Serbia return most of northern Macedonia, while demanding that Greece relinquish Salonika and southern Macedonia and abandon further claims to Adrianople. These demands struck directly at the principal gains of Serbia and Greece in the First Balkan War and were rejected. Serbia also had to prevent Bulgarian forces from cutting the connection between Skopje and the Serbian interior along the Vardar; Greece needed to secure Salonika, Kavala and the roads into southern Macedonia; and Montenegro sought restoration of the Sandžak and Metohija. Romania also maintained longstanding territorial claims against Austria-Hungary over southern Transylvania, so a deteriorating Balkan balance gave it an opportunity to pressure Bulgaria along the Danube. Germany and Austria-Hungary supported Bulgaria diplomatically, while Russia, concerned that hostilities might reach Constantinople, emphasized restraint. The weakening of the Ottoman Empire in Europe also made the retention of Adrianople and the prevention of a Greek advance eastward important elements in the military calculations of all sides.
impact: 這場戰爭沒有改變歐洲列強的整體邊界，卻徹底改變了三個巴爾干國家的實力位置。保加利亞雖保住亞德里安堡、西部色雷與皮林馬其頓，卻失去藉戰爭取得薩洛尼卡及打通愛琴海出口的可能；戰敗所引發的政治危機又使費迪南德一世於九月退位，由鮑里斯三世繼位。塞爾維亞因此成為中巴爾干最大的陸軍國家，取得從瓦爾達爾河上游通向斯科普里的戰略縱深；希臘則把薩洛尼卡變成面向愛琴海的主要軍港與交通中心，卻未能取得阿德里安堡，東色雷的歸屬仍然懸而未決。塞、希兩國在共同作戰時合作順暢，戰勝後卻立即因邊界、鐵路出口與馬其頓的安排形成新的競爭。黑山鞏固了通往塞爾維亞的內陸通道，羅馬尼亞則取得南多布魯加並增強對奧匈帝國施壓的地位；南特蘭西瓦尼亞仍未成為羅馬尼亞領土，相關要求因此延續到下一次危機。鄂圖曼帝國在歐洲的領土則退縮至東色雷，其原先橫跨巴爾干的統治結構至此近乎瓦解。這些結果一方面削弱保加利亞，另一方面使塞爾維亞、希臘與羅馬尼亞的軍力與外交地位上升，也把阿德里安堡及馬其頓邊界變成下一次巴爾干危機的實際爭端。
impactEn: The war did not alter the general frontier established by the European powers, but it transformed the practical position of three Balkan states. Bulgaria retained Adrianople, western Thrace and Pirin Macedonia, yet lost any realistic possibility of acquiring Salonika or opening an Aegean outlet through war; the political crisis produced by defeat also led Ferdinand I to abdicate in September and surrender the throne to Boris III. Serbia became the largest land power in the central Balkans and obtained a strategic depth extending along the upper Vardar toward Skopje. Greece turned Salonika into its principal military port and transport centre facing the Aegean, but did not obtain Adrianople, leaving the status of eastern Thrace unresolved. Serbia and Greece had cooperated effectively against a common enemy, but their rivalry over frontiers, rail access and the Macedonian settlement became visible immediately after victory. Montenegro consolidated an inland route toward Serbia, while Romania gained southern Dobruja and increased its leverage against Austria-Hungary. Southern Transylvania did not become Romanian territory, so that claim persisted into the next crisis. Ottoman rule in Europe contracted to eastern Thrace, and the former trans-Balkan Ottoman structure was thereby reduced almost to a remnant. The result weakened Bulgaria while raising the military and diplomatic weight of Serbia, Greece and Romania, and turned Adrianople and the Macedonian borders into concrete points of contention in the next Balkan crisis.
result: 8月10日簽訂的《布加勒斯特條約》確定了軍事失敗所帶來的領土安排。塞爾維亞取得以斯科普里、什蒂普與韋萊斯為核心的中部及北部馬其頓；希臘保住薩洛尼卡並取得南部馬其頓，範圍包括基爾基斯、塞雷斯、德米爾希薩爾與卡瓦拉一帶；黑山取得梅托希亞及桑扎克的一部分；羅馬尼亞取得南多布魯加，羅軍並於8月18日占領圖爾圖卡亞，隨後接管條約所劃定的地區。保加利亞仍保有皮林馬其頓、阿德里安堡與西部色雷，卻放棄進一步索取馬其頓與阿德里安堡的權利，並依條約向塞爾維亞支付五千萬法郎、向希臘支付三千萬法郎的賠款，軍隊上限被限制為十萬人。塞軍推進至斯科普里、什蒂普與韋萊斯，希軍控制薩洛尼卡及南部馬其頓的主要城鎮，黑山軍進入新獲地區，保軍則依協議撤往保加利亞本土及保留疆界。最後的結果是保加利亞企圖以武力修改《倫敦條約》的行動失敗，塞爾維亞與希臘保住第一次巴爾干戰爭的大部分收穫，黑山取得新土，羅馬尼亞成為最後加入而仍獲得土地的一方；保加利亞則付出賠款、軍力限制與喪失愛琴海出口的代價。
resultEn: The Bucharest Treaty signed on 10 August fixed the territorial consequences of Bulgaria’s military defeat. Serbia received central and northern Macedonia centred on Skopje, Štip and Veles. Greece retained Salonika and acquired southern Macedonia, including the Kilkis, Serres, Demir Hisar and Kavala areas. Montenegro obtained Metohija and part of the Sandžak. Romania received southern Dobruja; Romanian troops occupied Turtucaia on 18 August and subsequently took control of the area assigned by the treaty. Bulgaria retained Pirin Macedonia, Adrianople and western Thrace, but renounced any further claim to Macedonia and Adrianople. It agreed to pay Serbia 50 million francs and Greece 30 million francs in indemnity, and its army was limited to 100,000 men. Serbian forces advanced to Skopje, Štip and Veles; Greek troops held Salonika and the principal towns of southern Macedonia; Montenegrin units entered their new territories; and Bulgarian troops withdrew toward the Bulgarian interior and the frontiers left to them. Bulgaria’s attempt to revise the London Treaty by force therefore failed. Serbia and Greece preserved most of their First Balkan War gains, Montenegro secured additional territory, and Romania, although it entered last, also obtained land. Bulgaria, by contrast, paid indemnity, accepted a military limit and lost the prospect of an Aegean outlet.
